title: How Jones came to work with Ellington: Mercer's band
summary: Duke phoned at odd hours with propositions; Jones's first writing was for Mercer Ellington's Decca band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: At the end of the other tape we were talking about some of Norman Granz's recording projects and his labels, and we were trying to think of the name of Verve Records.

That Norman sold to MGM. You were talking about all the different Ellington sidemen that you recorded with and wrote for, and that you feel that's the way your work came to Duke's attention. How did it progress from there? How did you happen to get involved with Duke Ellington?

Oh, let's see. It's kind of hard to put that together. I have some hazy moments in my memory, but if anybody knows Ellington, how he can call you at two or three o'clock in the morning wherever you are, but he's wide awake.
And he'll give you a proposition when your mind is not quite together, you know?

And it started that way, in that direction. For instance, oh, the first writing I did was with Mercer Ellington. Mercer had the band, recorded on Decca Records. I wrote some, Billy Strayhorn wrote some, Mercer wrote some.
Was that the one, 'Stepping In Swing Society,' I think they called the album? It was recorded --
It had something to do with colors.
Oh. Then that's not the same one.
